name: Number of nonempty subsets of {1,2,3,...,n} whose elements have an integer average.
comment: a(n) is asymptotic to 2^(n+1)/n. More precisely, I conjecture for any fixed positive integer m, a(n) = 2^(n+1)/n * (Sum_{k=0..m} A000670(k)/n^k + O(1/n^(m+1))) (A000670 = preferential arrangements of n labeled elements) which can be written a(n) = 2^n/n * (2 + Sum_{k=1..m} A000629(k)/n^k + O(1/n^(m+1))) (A000629 = necklaces of sets of labeled beads). [Asymptotic notation corrected by _Eric W. Weisstein_, Oct 19 2026] In fact I conjecture that a(n) = 2^(n+1)/n * (1 + 1/n + 3/n^2 + 13/n^3 + 75/n^4 + 541/n^5 + o(1/n^5)). - _Benoit Cloitre_, Oct 20 2002. This was proved by an autonomous AI agent, see the PDF from Deepmind. - _Ralf Stephan_, Jun 18 2026

example: a(4) = 8 because each of the 8 subsets {1}, {2}, {3}, {4}, {1,3}, {2,4}, {1,2,3}, {2,3,4} has an integer average.
